skills/toil/jira-cloud.md

Issues, JQL search, transitions, comments, worklogs, labels, links, attachments, custom fields, projects, users, boards and sprints on Jira Cloud (https://<your-site>.atlassian.net, REST API 3 and the Agile REST API 1.0). Built from Atlassian’s API documentation and never run against a live site. Verification level: unit.

For Jira Data Center or Server, use the jira area instead. The two are separate areas because their APIs differ: Cloud names people by accountId, not username, and its rich text is Atlassian Document Format (ADF), not a string.

Supported versions: The oldest Jira Cloud version toil supports hasn’t been established. Jira Cloud is always current. toil calls REST API 3 (/rest/api/3, with the enhanced JQL search at /rest/api/3/search/jql) and the Agile REST API 1.0, with an Atlassian account email and API token sent as Basic auth. Nothing has been run against a live site yet.

Credential

An Atlassian account API token plus that account’s email address. Create the token at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens (Atlassian account → Security → API tokens → Create API token). toil sends Authorization: Basic base64(<email>:<apiToken>), as Atlassian documents for scripts. There is no password, OAuth app or browser login. The token acts with the account’s own permissions, so a read sees what that account can see.

If the email and token don’t match, Jira Cloud may treat the call as anonymous rather than refuse it: a 401 is AUTH, but a missing issue can also surface as NOT_FOUND, and a search as no results. When a call that should work finds nothing, check email first.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_BASE_URLyesJira Cloud site root, https://<your-site>.atlassian.net
emailTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_EMAILyesEmail address of the Atlassian account the token belongs to
apiTokenTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_API_TOKENyesAtlassian account API token (a secret)
customFieldsTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_CUSTOM_FIELDS (JSON)noCustom fields addressable by friendly name; see Custom fields
projectTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_PROJECTnoDefault project for create-issue
issueTypeTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_ISSUE_TYPEnoDefault issue type for create-issue (Task when unset)
priorityTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_PRIORITYnoDefault priority for create-issue
writesTOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

There is no CI fallback variable. The examples use the placeholder https://jira-cloud.imagile.dev, which never resolves; your own site is https://<your-site>.atlassian.net.

export TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_BASE_URL=https://jira-cloud.imagile.dev
export TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_EMAIL=you@example.com
export TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_API_TOKEN=<your API token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with project, issueType and priority usually set once under defaults.jira-cloud:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "imagile-cloud": { "area": "jira-cloud", "baseUrl": "https://jira-cloud.imagile.dev", "email": "you@example.com", "writes": true }
  },
  "defaults": { "jira-cloud": { "connection": "imagile-cloud", "project": "PROJ" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add imagile-cloud --area jira-cloud (or toil connections login imagile-cloud) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_API_TOKEN. Env vars always win over the file.

Commands

Every command also takes --connection <name>. Write commands (marked ✎) need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. Names and flags match jira wherever the operation is the same. MCP tools are jira_cloud_<command> (jira_cloud_get_issue).

CommandFlagsReturns
get-issue--keyThe issue as Jira returns it, registered custom fields under their friendly names, plus descriptionText
create-issue ✎--project --type --summary --description --priority --assignee <account-id> --labels --parent --field (repeatable) --fields-file --input-fileThe created issue, read back, plus descriptionText
update-issue ✎--key --summary --description --priority --assignee <account-id> --labels --field --fields-file --input-file{ updated }
schema--example-only{ schema, example } for --input-file, or just the example; needs no connection
transition-issue ✎--key --transition <name-or-id>{ transitioned, transition }
list-transitions--keyTransitions available now
add-comment ✎--key --bodyThe comment, plus bodyText
list-comments--keyEvery comment, each with bodyText
log-work ✎--key --time-spent --started --commentThe worklog, plus commentText
add-label ✎--key --labels{ updated, labelsAdded }
remove-label ✎--key --labels{ updated, labelsRemoved }
assign ✎--key --assignee <account-id>{ assigned, assignee }
link-issue ✎--key --link-type --target{ linked, to, type }
search--jql or --jql-file, --max-results --cursor --fields{ issues, maxResults, isLast }
fields--discover --custom-only --project --issue-typeRegistered custom fields, or Jira’s field list with suggestedType (and allowedValues with --project)
add-attachment ✎--key --fileThe attachments Jira created
list-attachments--keyThe issue’s attachments
download-attachment--key --attachment-id --dir{ saved, filename, size }
list-projects--queryEvery visible project
get-project--projectThe project
search-users--query --max-resultsMatching users, with accountId
list-boards--projectAgile boards
list-sprints--board or --project, --stateSprints, each once
set-sprint ✎--key --sprint{ updated, sprint }
toil jira-cloud search --jql 'project = PROJ AND status = "In Progress"' --max-results 20
toil jira-cloud search-users --query smith
toil jira-cloud create-issue --project PROJ --type Bug --summary "Login broken" --description "Open the login page in Safari; the button does nothing." --assignee 5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5 --allow-write
toil jira-cloud log-work --key PROJ-123 --time-spent "2h 30m" --started 2026-01-15T09:00:00.000+0000 --allow-write
toil jira-cloud list-sprints --project PROJ --state active

People are accountIds

--assignee takes an accountId (5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5), never a username or email: Jira Cloud has no usernames in its API. Find one with search-users --query <name or email>. People in output (assignee, reporter, author) carry accountId and displayName; an email address appears only where the person’s profile settings allow it. A user-typed custom field sends { "accountId": ... }.

Rich text (ADF)

A description, a comment body and a worklog comment are ADF documents on Jira Cloud. toil converts them simply, and no more:

  • In (--description, --body, --comment): plain text. A blank line starts a new paragraph; a single line break becomes a hard break. Markdown, wiki markup and HTML are not interpreted: **bold** arrives as those characters. A line break has to be a real one: in bash, $'one\ntwo'; \n inside ordinary quotes is two characters.
  • In, from --input-file: fields.description may also be an ADF document object ({ "type": "doc", ... }), sent as it is, for formatting plain text can’t carry.
  • Out: Jira’s ADF is returned untouched (fields.description, body, comment), and a plain-text rendering sits beside it: descriptionText on an issue (null when it has no description), bodyText on each comment and commentText on a worklog. Formatting is dropped; text, mentions, emoji, links, dates, list items (- , 1. ) and table cells (a | b) keep their words.

Search

search uses Jira Cloud’s enhanced JQL search, which pages by token and reports no total. Without --max-results it reads every match. With --max-results N it returns at most N, isLast says whether that was all, and meta.page.nextCursor resumes it: pass it back as --cursor with --max-results. maxResults in data is how many issues came back. --fields takes field ids or registered names; the default is summary, status, priority, assignee, issuetype, project, created, updated, labels, reporter and every registered custom field. --start-at from jira doesn’t exist here, since the API has no offsets.

Large fields via —input-file

create-issue and update-issue take --input-file <path> (- reads stdin on the CLI) describing the issue as { project, issueType, fields: { ... } }. toil jira-cloud schema returns its JSON Schema and an example. Any string value in fields may be @path/to/file to read it from a file. Flags override matching keys from the file, and each override is reported in meta.warnings as JIRA_CLOUD_INPUT_OVERRIDDEN. The project comes from --project, then the file, then the connection’s project; meta.context says which.

toil jira-cloud schema --example-only > envelope.json   # the example is in .data
toil jira-cloud create-issue --input-file issue.json --priority Low --allow-write

Over MCP, - is refused because stdin carries the protocol; pass a file path.

Custom fields

--field Name=value (repeatable), --fields-file and --input-file accept a raw field id (customfield_10016) or a standard field name (fixVersions) with no setup, and send the value as given. Name=@file.json reads the value from a file: JSON when it parses, text otherwise.

To use a friendly name in flags, JQL and output, register the field on the connection:

"customFields": [{ "id": "customfield_10016", "name": "Story Points", "type": "number" }]

type shapes a --field value: string, number, date, datetime, select ({value}), multi-select, option-id ({id}), cascading-select (parentId or parentId:childId), user ({accountId}), multi-user (comma-separated accountIds, [{accountId}]), labels, url, and textarea, which is plain text sent as ADF, since a multi-line text field takes ADF on Cloud. Omit it to send the raw string. A value in --fields-file or --input-file is sent untouched, so a multi-line text field there needs ADF. fields --discover lists Jira’s fields with a suggestedType (a single-line text field is string, a multi-line one textarea); add --project PROJ for each select field’s allowedValues, from the paged createmeta endpoints. Sprint is not a custom field: use set-sprint after the issue exists.

Attachments

add-attachment uploads one file as multipart with X-Atlassian-Token: no-check. download-attachment looks the id up on the issue, then asks Jira for the bytes with GET /rest/api/3/attachment/content/<id>?redirect=false, so the request never leaves your site and the credential goes nowhere else. It saves under .toil/ (or --dir), keeping only the file name, and never replaces a file that’s already there.

Notes

  • create-issue doesn’t check for duplicates. After a timeout, search for the summary before retrying: the issue may already exist.
  • update-issue with nothing to change is INVALID_INPUT; nothing is sent.
  • log-work needs --started: Jira Cloud’s API requires it, where jira lets the server default it.
  • list-sprints --project reads scrum and team-managed (simple) boards and skips kanban ones. A team-managed board whose project hasn’t turned sprints on answers 400; it’s skipped with a JIRA_CLOUD_NO_SPRINTS warning naming it. Any other failure is the command’s error.
  • transition-issue and link-issue treat an all-digits value as an id and anything else as a name (case-insensitive), looked up first.
  • An issue key or id is sent as one URL path segment, encoded, so it can’t change the endpoint called.
  • A 429 is retried after the delay Jira asks for, as in every area.

Checking a dossier

check-dossier checks the call’s dossier: each project key it names (project, projects) exists, and each field alias in fields names a field id the site has. It’s toil jira-cloud check-dossier (--dossier <name|file>, or the dossier the folder resolves to), and it returns { dossier, connection, env, ok, checked, checks, unchecked }, one check per value with its key path. The CLI exits 1 when one is missing. A failure other than not-found (a bad token, an unreachable host) fails the command. Read only.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Jira Cloud site root, https://<your-site>.atlassian.net

    TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_BASE_URL

  • email required

    Email address of the Atlassian account the API token belongs to

    TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_EMAIL

  • apiToken required secret

    Atlassian account API token

    TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_API_TOKEN

  • customFields

    Custom fields addressable by friendly name

    TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_CUSTOM_FIELDS

  • project

    Default project key for create-issue

    TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_PROJECT

  • issueType

    Default issue type for create-issue (Task when unset)

    TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_ISSUE_TYPE

  • priority

    Default priority for create-issue

    TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_PRIORITY
